Green Algorithms: Quantifying the Carbon Footprint of Computation: Reading-scope warrant imported from the field model; not verification of this organizing row or exact semantic correspondence.
Estimating the Carbon Footprint of BLOOM: Reading-scope warrant imported from the field model; not verification of this organizing row or exact semantic correspondence.
Quantization and Training of Neural Networks for Efficient Integer-Arithmetic-Only Inference: Reading-scope warrant imported from the field model; not verification of this organizing row or exact semantic correspondence.
Efficient Guided Generation for Large Language Models: Abstract inspected: finite-state constrained generation with regular expressions and context-free grammars; not semantic correctness.
Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning: Federated learning survey; source scope and abstract inspected, not an assertion-level crosswalk.
The worst-case execution-time problem: overview of methods and survey of tools: Execution-time bounds and timing-analysis assumptions; narrow timing reference, not a whole physical-system safety case.
Apache Parquet file format: Describes row groups, column chunks, metadata, and selective sequential column reading; one concrete storage-layout design. Reading basis, not independent assertion validation.
Apache Beam programming guide: Pipeline I/O: Defines reading from and writing to external sources through pipeline I/O transforms; adapters differ in behavior. Reading basis, not independent assertion validation.
Apache Iceberg specification: Schema evolution: Describes adding/deleting/renaming/reordering fields, permitted type promotions, schema IDs, and compatibility mechanisms for that format. Reading basis, not independent assertion validation.
The Oracle Problem in Software Testing: A Survey: Author-hosted paper distinguishing desired from incorrect observed behavior; includes specifications, partial oracles, metamorphic relations, and human judgment. Reading basis, not independent assertion validation.
Google SRE: Testing for Reliability: Defines integration/system tests and discusses statistical fault-oriented testing; passing tests does not prove reliability. Reading basis, not independent assertion validation.
Principles of Chaos Engineering: Authors describe experiments with disruptive events, observable steady-state hypotheses, and containing experimental impact; production experiments are not required by our concept. Reading basis, not independent assertion validation.
MLflow: Managing Dependencies in Models: Documents model environment metadata, dependencies, direct/transitive version locking, and inference limitations; locking does not guarantee identical execution. Reading basis, not independent assertion validation.
Kubeflow Pipelines: Pipeline concepts: Describes component ordering, conditions, parameters/artifacts, caching, retries, and orchestration; an implementation example rather than a universal DAG requirement. Reading basis, not independent assertion validation.
PyTorch: Reproducibility: States limits across versions/platforms and distinguishes randomness controls, algorithm determinism, and associated performance tradeoffs. Reading basis, not independent assertion validation.
CUDA Programming Guide: Programming Model: A vendor example of accelerator execution and memory organization; not a universal accelerator definition.
NVIDIA System Management Interface documentation: Vendor-specific power limits, thermal slowdown, and operating telemetry; not a physical-system safety qualification.
MLSysBook hardware acceleration and physical placement: Internal manuscript reading basis: Volume I hardware acceleration, Volume II compute infrastructure, and Volume IV placement. Electrical and thermal scope remains draft.
Google SRE book: Service Level Objectives: SLI/SLO/error-budget vocabulary for requirements rows.
The Datacenter as a Computer: Designing Warehouse-Scale Machines, 3rd ed.: Canonical textbook for warehouse-scale facilities, power, cooling, networking, storage, and cluster management.
MIT 6.5940 TinyML and Efficient Deep Learning Computing, Fall 2024: Curriculum warrant for efficient models, long context, and edge/embedded hardware.
Stanford CS149 Parallel Computing, Fall 2025: Curriculum warrant for parallel speedup reasoning, hardware specialization, and mapping AI to datacenters.
CMU 11-868 LLM Systems, Spring 2025: Curriculum warrant for MoE, efficient attention, and LLM training/inference systems.
UT Austin CS 378 Systems for ML, Fall 2024: Curriculum warrant for collectives, compilers, linear attention, and SSMs.
UW CSE 599o, Autumn 2025: Curriculum warrant for GPU communication, interconnects, data loading, and N-D parallelism.
Huyen, Designing Machine Learning Systems: Production-ML lifecycle comparison (data, deployment, monitoring, continual learning); table of contents inspected.
Kästner, Machine Learning in Production: Software-engineering lifecycle and operations comparison.
Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback: Canonical description of the SFT-reward-model-RLHF post-training pipeline.
Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters: Defines the test-time compute allocation problem and its main mechanisms.
TensorFlow Lite Micro: Embedded Machine Learning on TinyML Systems: On-device runtime design and deployment constraints.
MLPerf Inference Benchmark: System benchmarking methodology (scenarios
MITRE ATLAS: Adversary technique taxonomy for AI systems; comparison for attack and supply-chain rows.
Silent Data Corruptions at Scale: Reading-scope warrant for hardware-fault and SDC row.
A higher order estimate of the optimum checkpoint interval for restart dumps: Reading-scope warrant for checkpoint interval and restart economics.
Chasing Carbon: The Elusive Environmental Footprint of Computing: Reading-scope warrant for embodied carbon and hardware lifecycle.
Sustainable AI: Environmental Implications, Challenges and Opportunities: Reading-scope warrant for ML-specific environmental accounting across the lifecycle.
Leveson, Engineering a Safer World: Systems Thinking Applied to Safety: Canonical text for system-theoretic hazard analysis (STPA).
ISO 26262-1:2018 Road vehicles: Functional safety: Functional-safety standard scoping hazard analysis, integrity levels, and the safety lifecycle.
ISO 21448:2022 Road vehicles: Safety of the intended functionality: Standard scoping hazards from functional insufficiency of perception and learned components.
UL 4600 Standard for Safety for the Evaluation of Autonomous Products (Koopman overview): Autonomy safety-case standard scoping safety cases and field indicators.
Goal Structuring Notation Community Standard: Reference notation for structured safety arguments.
Concrete Problems in AI Safety: Widely taught statement of ML-specific accident risks.
The Safety Filter: A Unified View of Safety-Critical Control in Autonomous Systems: Survey scoping runtime safety filters.
Control Barrier Functions: Theory and Applications: Reference for barrier-function enforcement.
Sha, Using Simplicity to Control Complexity: Origin of the Simplex runtime-assurance architecture.
A Survey of Algorithms for Black-Box Safety Validation of Cyber-Physical Systems: Survey scoping falsification and rare-failure validation.
Algorithms for Verifying Deep Neural Networks: Survey scoping neural-network verification.
Kalra and Paddock, Driving to Safety (RAND RR-1478): Standard argument on the statistics of demonstrating rare-failure safety.
Barocas, Hardt, Narayanan, Fairness and Machine Learning: Textbook scoping fairness criteria and mitigation.
Inherent Trade-Offs in the Fair Determination of Risk Scores: Canonical incompatibility result for fairness criteria.
Molnar, Interpretable Machine Learning: Widely used reference scoping explainability methods.
Model Cards for Model Reporting: Origin of model-documentation practice.
Datasheets for Datasets: Origin of dataset-documentation practice.
Bainbridge, Ironies of Automation: Canonical human-factors account of supervising automation.
Parasuraman and Riley, Humans and Automation: Use, Misuse, Disuse, Abuse: Canonical account of automation bias and complacency.
Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act): Primary risk-tiered AI regulation.
Closing the AI Accountability Gap: Defining an End-to-End Framework for Internal Algorithmic Auditing: Reference framework for algorithmic audits.
Anthropic, Effective Context Engineering for AI Agents: Practitioner reference scoping context engineering.
MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems: Reference design for tiered agent memory.
Model Context Protocol specification: De facto standard tool-discovery protocol.
Anthropic, Building Effective Agents: Practitioner reference scoping agent loops, workflows, and orchestration.
ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models: Canonical agent-loop pattern.
Temporal documentation: Reference implementation of durable execution and replay.
Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?: Empirical taxonomy scoping multi-agent failure.
AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation: Widely used multi-agent orchestration framework.
Past, Present, and Future of Simultaneous Localization and Mapping: Survey scoping state estimation and mapping.
BEVFusion: Multi-Task Multi-Sensor Fusion with Unified Bird’s-Eye View Representation: Representative learned sensor-fusion system.
MIT Robotic Manipulation (Tedrake): Course scoping robot perception, planning, and control.
Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models (DreamerV3): Representative learned world model.
LaValle, Planning Algorithms: Textbook scoping motion planning.
Rawlings, Mayne, Diehl, Model Predictive Control: Theory, Computation, and Design: Textbook scoping MPC.
Scheduling Algorithms for Multiprogramming in a Hard-Real-Time Environment: Foundational real-time scheduling result.
Preemptive Scheduling of Multi-criticality Systems with Varying Degrees of Execution Time Assurance: Origin of mixed-criticality scheduling.
RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control: Origin of the vision-language-action model category.
pi0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control: Representative generalist robot foundation model.
Domain Randomization for Transferring Deep Neural Networks from Simulation to the Real World: Canonical sim-to-real technique.

title: Community
text:
GLOBAL NETWORK
  
  Machine Learning Systems is taught at universities across five continents, from Bogotá to Johannesburg, from Kobe to Nairobi. Every chapter and lab is open and free, and we ship hardware kits to partner universities that need them.

title: Community
text:
How We Reach Learners
Every chapter is free to read, but access means more than a URL. It means hardware, training, and showing up in person.

  


  
    
    Hardware Where It Is Needed
    We ship real hardware (Arduino and Seeed edge devices) to partner universities that could not otherwise afford them. Students learn on real silicon, not just simulations.
  
  
    
    Workshops on the Ground
    The annual SciTinyML workshop series at ICTP in Trieste brings researchers and students together to apply ML to scientific challenges, from environmental monitoring to health diagnostics. Regional editions run across Latin America and Africa.
  
  
    
    Instructor Support
    Partner universities receive curriculum materials, lecture slides, and mentorship. The TinyML4D network connects educators across institutions so no one is teaching alone.
  
  
    
    Free and Open, Always
    The textbook is free to read online. The edX Professional Certificate reaches hundreds of thousands of learners. The textbook is free under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, and the teaching materials under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
